messages.body_plain:
Was the new version released to enable the embed options of open source Shiny page?

regards

On Wednesday, 26 April 2017 22:50:51 UTC+5:30, Alexander Poon wrote:
>
> I'm running Shiny Server Open Source on Ubuntu 16.10. My organization's IT department tells me I need to set X-Frame-Options, so following the docs (http://docs.rstudio.com/shiny-server/#frame_options) I edited /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf as follows:
>
> # Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
>
> run_as shiny;
>
>
> # Set x-frame-options
>
> frame_options deny;
>
>
> # Define a server that listens on port 3838
>
> server {
>
>   listen 3838;
>
>
>   # Define a location at the base URL
>
>   location / {
>
>
>     # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
>
>     site_dir /srv/shiny-server;
>
>
>     # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
>
>     log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
>
>
>     # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
>
>     # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
>
>     directory_index on;
>
>   }
>
> }
>
> After editing shiny-server.conf I ran sudo systemctl kill -s HUP -kill-who=main shiny-server.
>
> However, when I pull up Developer Tools on my Shiny app, I don't see X-Frame-Options: deny under Response Headers. Is this what I should be looking at to see that I did it right?
>
> I also tried putting frame_options under server and got the same (lack of) result.
>
messages.body_snippet:
Was the new version released to enable the embed options of open source Shiny page?

regards

messages.body_plain:
rm(list=ls())
library(shiny)
#ui
#shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
ui <- fluidPage(

  headerPanel("Application Name"),
  sidebarLayout(

    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput("slider1", label = "Period:", min = 1, max=100, value = 25 ),
      sliderInput("slider2", label = "On hand Inventory1:", min = 0, max=qpois(0.9999,0.57), value = 0),
      sliderInput("slider3", label = "On hand Inventory2:", min=0, max=qpois(0.9999,1.53), value = 0),
      sliderInput("slider4", label = "On hand Inventory3:", min=0, max=qpois(0.9999,3.14), value = 0),
      # selectInput("obs", label = "Lambda:", choices = c(0.5,1.5,3), selected = 0.5 ),
      numericInput("obs" , label = "price1", value = 10 , min = 1, max = 1400,step = 1),
      numericInput("obs" , label = "price1", value = 10 , min = 1, max = 120,step = 1),
      numericInput("obs" , label = "price1", value = 10 , min = 1, max = 20,step = 1)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("demand")

    )
  )
)

server = function(input,output) {

  output$demand<- renderPlot ({
    simlenght=input$slider1; y1=input$slider2; y2=input$slider3; y3=input$slider4;
    p[1]=numericInput$price1; p[2]=numericInput$price2; p[3]=numericInput$price3;
    nu.rep=1;h=0.25; p=rep(1:3); C=c(1072,88.72,12.16);lambda=c(0.57,1.53,3.14);
    LT=0;LeadT=3;palette_load=c(4,60,960);

    holdcost1=(h/52)*C[1]               #holding cost rate*price of the product
    holdcost2=(h/52)*C[2]
    holdcost3=(h/52)*C[3]

    gama1=p[1]/(holdcost1+p[1])
    gama2=p[2]/(holdcost2+p[2])
    gama3=p[3]/(holdcost3+p[3])

    s1=qpois(gama1,lambda[1]*LeadT)
    s2=qpois(gama2,lambda[2]*LeadT)
    s3=qpois(gama3,lambda[3]*LeadT)

    alpha=c(1/palette_load)

    while(nu.rep<=100)
    {

      demand1=rpois(simlenght,0.57) #deman of product 1
      demand2=rpois(simlenght,1.53) #deman of product 2    #match elements and alpha
      demand3=rpois(simlenght,3.14)   #deman of product 3

      x1=x2=x3=rep(0,simlenght)                                #order size
      y1=y2=y3=rep(0,simlenght)                               #inventory level

      tempx1=tempx2=tempx3=rep(0,simlenght)
      holdingcost1=holdingcost2=holdingcost3=rep(0,simlenght)
      ordercost1=ordercost2=ordercost3=rep(0,simlenght)
      revenue1=revenue2=revenue3=rep(0,simlenght)
      profit1=profit2=profit3=rep(0,simlenght)
      sale1=sale2=sale3=rep(0,simlenght)
      totalorder=rep(0,simlenght)

      sale1[1]=sale2[1]=sale3[1]=0;

      inv1=x1+y1
      inv2=x2+y2
      inv3=x3+y3

      y1[2]=s1
      y2[2]=s2
      y3[2]=s3

      inv1[2]=s1
      inv2[2]=s2
      inv3[2]=s3

      x1[1]=x2[1]=x3[1]=1;

      t=2
      for (t in c(2:100))
      {

        tempx1[t]=max(0,s1-inv1[t])     #order=order up to level - inventory position
        tempx2[t]=max(0,s2-inv2[t])
        tempx3[t]=max(0,s3-inv3[t])

        totalorder = totalorder + tempx1[t]*alpha[1] + tempx1[t]*alpha[2] + tempx1[t]*alpha[3]

        if ((totalorder>0.95))
        {
          x1[t]=max(0,s1-inv1[t])     #order=order up to level - inventory position
          x2[t]=max(0,s2-inv2[t])
          x3[t]=max(0,s3-inv3[t])

          totalorder=0

        }

        #SALE
        sale1[t]=min(demand1[t],y1[t]+ x1[t-LT])
        sale2[t]=min(demand2[t],y2[t]+ x2[t-LT])
        sale3[t]=min(demand3[t],y3[t]+ x3[t-LT])

        #UPDATE
        inv1[t+1]=inv1[t]+x1[t]-sale1[t]    #inventory position after sale
        inv2[t+1]=inv2[t]+x2[t]-sale2[t]
        inv3[t+1]=inv3[t]+x3[t]-sale3[t]

        y1[t+1] = max(0,y1[t] - sale1[t] + x1[t-LT])     #inventory level after sale
        y2[t+1] = max(0,y2[t] - sale2[t] + x2[t-LT])
        y3[t+1] = max(0,y3[t] - sale3[t] + x3[t-LT])

        #COST
        ordercost1[t]=x1[t]*C[1]            #ordering cost = order*price of product
        ordercost2[t]=x2[t]*C[2]
        ordercost3[t]=x3[t]*C[3]

        holdingcost1[t]=y1[t]*holdcost1     #holding cost=inventory on hand * holding cost
        holdingcost2[t]=y2[t]*holdcost2
        holdingcost3[t]=y3[t]*holdcost3

        revenue1[t]=sale1[t]*p[1]            #revenue=sale*sales price
        revenue2[t]=sale2[t]*p[2]
        revenue3[t]=sale3[t]*p[3]

        profit1[t]=revenue1[t]-ordercost1[t]-holdingcost1[t]
        profit2[t]=revenue2[t]-ordercost2[t]-holdingcost2[t]
        profit3[t]=revenue3[t]-ordercost3[t]-holdingcost3[t]

        sumprofit[t]=profit1[t]+profit2[t]+profit3[t]
      }

    }

    t=c(1:100)
    plot(tsumprofit[t],t,type = "l")

  })

}

shinyApp(ui=ui, server=server)

messages.subject: "Permission denied" error when accessing external executable
messages.subject_clean: "Permission denied" error when accessing external executable
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I run a shiny app with TreeTagger (linguistic parser). The app passes a character vector to function treetag() (part of the koRpus package), which then accesses the external TreeTagger installation, which is included in the app directory. Everything runs perfectly locally. However, on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, I get the following error message:

"An error has occurred. Check your logs or contact the app author for clarification."

In the log file, it says:

"2019-05-28T15:14:22.927336+00:00 shinyapps[952518]: sh: 1: ./TreeTagger/bin/tree-tagger: Permission denied"

This is the path to the parser executable. It seems the permission is denied. Any suggestions?

I use Ubuntu 18.04, R version 3.4.4.

Thank you in advance.
